text: Prove that no lossless compressor shrinks every input. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: // Suppose a compressor shrinks every n-bit input by at least one bit.
// There are ___ inputs of length exactly n.
// The strings of length n-1 or less number ___ .
// and the decompressor cannot know which was meant. Contradiction.
explanation: Three lines, using Chapter 17's sum of powers of two for the third time. The conclusion is stronger than "some inputs do not shrink": for every lossless compressor, some inputs must *grow* — verified, with 200 of 200 random 64-byte inputs growing under gzip. Which is why every real compressor stores an incompressible block uncompressed with a flag, and that flag is the unavoidable growth minimised.
